title: Prophylaxis
subtitle: Ask what your opponent wants — then take it away.
goals: Find the opponent's best idea before your own
Spend a tempo to kill a plan permanently

steps.say: Nimzowitsch's great idea, and the habit that separates strong players from everyone else: before choosing your move, ask what your OPPONENT would play if it were their turn — then consider simply preventing it. A prophylactic move often looks like it does nothing. What it does is delete an entire plan from the position, permanently.

steps.prompt: Ask the prophylactic question: what does Black want? Then stop it!
hints: Black's most annoying idea is ...Ng4, hitting your e3 bishop and dragging your position around. Take the square away before he gets there.
h3 — one modest pawn move deletes ...Ng4 forever.

line.say: Prophylaxis. The move creates no threat and wins no material — it simply removes Black's most natural active idea from the board for the rest of the game. Nimzowitsch: 'the threat is stronger than the execution' applies to your opponent's threats too. Kill them before they exist.

rejections.say: Ambitious — and after ...Ng4! your bishop is harassed and the e4 pawn hangs. Grabbing space before dealing with the opponent's key square is how good positions collapse.
A natural developing move that walks into ...Ng4, when your bishop must move again. Ask what Black wants FIRST; the developing move will still be there next turn.

steps.wrongSay: Which black knight jump would irritate you most? Take that square away.
steps.successSay: The prophylactic question: 'what does he want?' Ask it every single move.

steps.prompt: Black's bishop on c5 eyes your king. Prevent the invasion before it starts!
hints: Black would love ...Bb4 or ...Ng4-e3 style ideas, and his bishop is the most annoying piece. Which pawn move takes squares from it?
a3 removes b4 from the bishop and prepares b4 to chase it entirely.

line.say: A quiet pawn move that takes b4 from the bishop and prepares to gain a tempo with b2–b4. Prophylaxis is rarely spectacular — it is a tempo spent to make your opponent's pieces worse for the next thirty moves.

rejections.say: A central advance that opens lines toward your own king while Black's pieces are the better placed. Before opening the position, remove the enemy's best-placed piece from its best square.
A capture that helps Black: ...Nxd5 activates his pieces and opens the e-file toward your king. Not every capture is progress — ask what it does for HIM.

steps.wrongSay: Take a square away from Black's most active piece.
steps.successSay: Prevention costs a tempo and saves a game. That is the trade prophylaxis always offers.

steps.say: Build the habit with three questions, in this order, every move: (1) What is my opponent threatening RIGHT NOW? (2) What does he want to do NEXT? (3) Only then — what do I want? Most blunders below master level come from skipping straight to question three.
